Subject: Checkout failures — urgent assistance needed

Sean,

We're seeing an elevated error rate and long tail latencies on Redwood-powered checkout calls starting ~08:45 PDT this morning. ~12% of checkout attempts are failing with 500/timeout and an additional 25% have token-level timeouts (>3s per token) which is impacting our conversions. Our engineers pulled a few logs and attached a short snippet (gridline_error_snippet.log).

Customer impact: nightly peak window traffic is being throttled or failing; we've already paused a promo that drove >20% traffic. We need an immediate plan: are you able to stand up an exec war-room and tell us ETA on mitigation?

Please escalate.

—Alex

Head of Engineering, Gridline Commerce

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Sep 2028 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout failures — immediate triage findings

Team — initial triage (results attached: initial_rpm_snapshot.csv):
- Symptom: token timeouts concentrated on the checkout model route (route: /v1/generate/checkout).
- Error breakdown: 58% 500s coming from model runtime OOM/retry; 32% from client timeouts due to token delay; remainder network retries.
- Throughput: observed drop in sustained TPS despite incoming traffic holding.

Hypothesis: recent quantization variant rolled to the route (yesterday evening) + heavier input sequence lengths from a new promo. Together these are increasing memory usage and causing frequent micro-restarts.

Short-term mitigations I suggest (we can apply within 10–20 minutes):
1) Temporarily pin route to the previous quantized variant (roll back model variant).
2) Apply prefix/KV cache priming for the checkout model for next hour.
3) Enable request-level throttling (graceful 429) for non-critical customers to reduce pressure.

I'll keep digging on traces; routing traces are on Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/gridline-checkout

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: initial_rpm_snapshot.csv (csv)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Sep 2028 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout failures — infra observations and immediate plan

Quick infra notes:
- Observed memory pressure (GPU VRAM) on pool rz-prod-a (nodes gpu-12..gpu-15). Kernel spiking correlates with sequences >1,200 tokens (checkout payload + context).
- Autoscaler is oscillating; cold starts + continuous batching causing queue depth to spike.

Immediate actions I'm executing now (ETA ~15–30m):
A) Pin route to previous model variant (Monica to confirm).
B) Drain and rolling-restart gpu-13 and gpu-14 with an updated kernel selection that reduces memory footprint (hotfix).
C) Temporarily divert Gridline traffic to dedicated reserved pool (dedicated-rl-4) we keep warm for high-priority customers — increases cost but preserves latency.

I've attached the short runbook excerpt I'm following: gpupool-rollout.txt. If rolling restart doesn't reduce errors, we will fail traffic to the dedicated pool and apply cache warmers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure & Runtime, Redwood Inference
Attachment: gpupool-rollout.txt (text)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@gridline.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Sep 2028 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gridline checkout — root cause, resolution, and next steps

Alex / team — final update and summary (post-fix):

Root cause: a late-night model-variant promotion (2028-09-05 22:15 PDT) enabled a new quantization pipeline that changed kernel selection heuristics. Under heavy promo inputs (longer prompts, nested contexts), the variant increased VRAM usage and triggered repeated micro-restarts.

What we did:
1) Immediately pinned the route back to the prior variant.
2) Rolled two GPU nodes with a kernel hotfix and applied KV cache priming.
3) Diverted a small percentage of traffic to a dedicated warm pool while validating stability.

Result: metrics normalized over the weekend — 99.8% successful checkout calls in the monitored window; tail latencies returned to baseline. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/gridline-checkout

Next steps / commitments:
- Postmortem: draft attached (postmortem-draft.md). We'll deliver a finalized postmortem and concrete mitigation plan (improved pre-rollout performance gating, tighter variance testing for quantization) by Sep 12.
- Commercial: our team pre-committed to an SLO credit scope; procurement will receive the formal statement of impact tomorrow.
- Action owner mapping: Laura (root cause & remediation), Karthik (runtime kernel changes & rollout plan), Monica (customer-facing telemetry & runbook updates), Sean (customer comms and exec liaison).

Thanks for patience — apologies for the impact. We're scheduling a 30-minute review with your eng leadership on Tue 9/11 to walk through the postmortem and prevention plan.

—Laura Bennett
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: postmortem-draft.md (markdown)
